title: The expected-prefix result is a lower bound in its stated low-risk regime
statement: For isotropic C~N(0,I_M/M), q<M exact residual reads and2^B q-subspace codewords, beta small-ball/union and random-Haar codebook integrals bound distortion, with high-rate exponent2/(M-q). Unequal-dimensional Grassmann rate-distortion and structured Cube-Split quantizers are established ancestry, not new discoveries or cheap random-codebook encoding. Separate exact-read expected-prefix theorem, d=m-q>0 and 0<R<d/m: B ln2 >=(d/2)[ln(d/(mR))-1+mR/d]. At R>=d/m this argument gives0, R=0 needs infinite expected length, d=0 is separate. Prefix framing is conditional on replay readouts/seeds, q remains HARD; mutual information conditions full replay V/seeds only after Gaussian residual identity. No exact expected-length value, noisy expected-prefix theorem, expected-query theorem or substitution of structured Hermite law for isotropic Gaussian is justified.

requires: For the expected-prefix theorem: isotropic Gaussian U,V independent, F=U^T V/sqrt(m), final decoder retains U/legal readouts, q<m exact V reads with HARD q cap, seeds independent.

Controller words prefix-free conditional on replay readouts/seeds, E length<=B; timing and stopping charged. Low-risk formula only0<R<(m-q)/m; above threshold bound0,zero-risk/diverging and d=0 endpoints separate.
